# ANU Linguistics Department

> A comprehensive digital archive of Australian indigenous language documentation, grammar resources, and linguistic research centered at the Australian National University.

The ANU Linguistics Department maintains extensive documentation of endangered Aboriginal languages from across Australia, with particular focus on languages from Central Australia, Northern Territory, and Western Australia. This resource serves as a critical repository for linguistic research and language preservation efforts.

## Key Topics

- Australian Aboriginal languages
- Language documentation
- Indigenous linguistics
- Endangered languages
- David Nash

## Department Overview

- [ANU Linguistics Department](https://www0.anu.edu.au/linguistics/): Main landing page and directory for the ANU Linguistics Department with access to all language resources and research archives

## Language Documentation & Resources

- [Mudburra Language](https://www0.anu.edu.au/linguistics/nash/aust/m/): Comprehensive grammar and documentation of Mudburra language from Northern Territory, including linguistic analysis and reference materials
- [Ngatjumaya Language](https://www0.anu.edu.au/linguistics/nash/aust/sewa/): Ngatjumaya language documentation and resources from South-East Western Australia with detailed linguistic records
- [Central Australia Regional Guide](https://www0.anu.edu.au/linguistics/nash/aust/ca/): Regional overview of Central Australian Aboriginal languages and associated linguistic resources and research materials
